Both integrate changes from one branch into another; differ in what happens to history.

`git merge feature`: creates merge commit with two parents, tying both histories together. Existing commits untouched → safe on shared branches. Cost: non-linear history, extra merge commits. `git rebase main` (from feature): replays your commits on top of `main` as new commits with new SHAs → linear history, no merge commit. Cost: rewrites history, conflicts resolved per replayed commit instead of once.

Gotcha: never rebase commits others have pulled. Their history diverges from yours, and you need a force push (`--force-with-lease`) to publish. Rule of thumb: rebase local/private branches to tidy up before sharing, merge to integrate into shared branches.
